newsitem.title: UK: Chile to adhere to targets before rate cut--Massad.
newsitem.headline: Chile to adhere to targets before rate cut--Massad.

text.p: Chile's central bank said on Monday it would consider cutting interest rates only after it was convinced the country was on track to meet key economic targets on inflation and gross domestic product growth.
"The adjustment process will end as soon as we see very clearly that we are in a secure role for 1997," Central Bank President Carlos Massad told a meeting of British financiers.
"The job of the central bank is to make certain that targets negotiated with the Ministry of Finance are fulfilled, both in terms of growth in the economy and in the rate of inflation," he said.
"We're on our way to meeting those targets for 1996 and we don't want to risk not meeting those targets."
The financial markets have been speculating on the chance of a cut in official interest rates before year-end. Massad declined comment when asked if he was ruling out any easing before then.

The central bank has been pursuing a restrictive monetary policy, known as an adjustment, for most of this year in an effort to cut inflation and reduce economic growth to around 7.0 ercent this year from over 8.0 percent in 1995.
Some analysts are concerned that delaying a rate cut may result in a sharper than expected economic slowdown.
